cards.text: This is a song by David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster. It starts simple: God arises.

cards.question: True or false: David says that when God arises, those who hate Him stand their ground.

cards.text: His enemies are scattered, and those who hate Him flee His presence. As smoke is blown away, God will drive them out, and as wax melts before the fire, the wicked will perish before Him.

cards.question: The wicked will perish like melting wax before God. But David says the righteous will do something very different before Him. What?

cards.text: Then David says to sing praises to God, the One who rides on the clouds, whose name is the LORD. Friend, my singing could crack a cookie in half, and I'm STILL joining in on this one.

cards.question: True or false: David says the God who rides on the clouds is also a defender of widows.

cards.text: God in His holy habitation is a father of the fatherless and a defender of widows. Friend, I miss the six little cookie cutters who used to call me Papa, so that line hits me right in the apron.

cards.question: Right after the fatherless and the widows, David turns to the lonely. What does God do for them?

cards.text: God leads prisoners out to prosperity, but the rebellious live in a sun-scorched land. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so I'll take the being-led-out part, thank you VERY much.
Now David looks back and talks right to God. He remembers when God went out before His people and marched through the wasteland.

cards.question: When God marched through the wasteland before His people, the earth ___ before Him.
The earth shook and the heavens poured down rain before God, the One on Sinai. Then He sent abundant rain. What does David say that rain did for God's weary inheritance?
God's flock settled in. From His bounty, who does David say God provided for?

cards.text: David's still singing about what God has done for His people. Now the Lord gives the command, and a great company of women proclaim it.

cards.question: A great company of women proclaims what the Lord commands. What do they say kings and their armies do?
In the women's song, kings and their armies flee in haste. What happens to the plunder they leave behind?

answers.text: It gets divided up at home
It gets burned on the spot
It gets sent back to them

cards.text: She who waits at home divides the plunder, like missing the whole office cookie swap and walking out with a box anyway. Then the song says that though you lie down among the sheepfolds, the dove's wings are covered with silver and her feathers with shimmering gold.
When the Almighty scattered the kings in the land, it was like the snow falling on Zalmon, a mountain. Then David turns to Mount Bashan, a mountain of God, a mountain of many peaks.

cards.question: David asks the mountains of many peaks why they gaze in envy. What are they gazing at?

answers.text: The mountain God chose to dwell on

cards.question: True or false: David says the LORD will surely dwell on His chosen mountain forever.
Then David pictures the chariots of God, and he gives a number. True or false: he says they number only in the hundreds.

cards.text: The chariots of God are tens of thousands, thousands of THOUSANDS. Friend, I lose count of the chocolate chips in ONE batch.
The Lord is in His sanctuary as He was at Sinai. Then David tells God that He has ascended on high, led captives away and received gifts from men, even from the rebellious.

cards.question: God has ascended on high, led captives away and received gifts, even from the rebellious. What does David say it's for?

answers.text: So the LORD God may dwell there
So the nations will fear Israel
So the priests will have plenty

cards.text: Then David blesses the Lord, who daily bears our burden, the God of our salvation. DAILY, friend, not just the big days, but the snooze-button, where-are-my-keys days too.

cards.question: David calls God the God of our salvation and a God of deliverance. How far does he say the Lord GOD's rescue reaches?
True or false: David says God will make peace with those who persist in guilty ways.

cards.text: David says God will surely crush the heads of His enemies, those who persist in guilty ways.

Then the Lord said He will retrieve them from Bashan and bring them up from the depths of the sea. The psalm says it's so that a foot may be dipped in the blood of the foes, and the tongues of dogs too.
Now David pictures a parade. He says they have seen God's procession, as his God and King marches into the sanctuary.

cards.question: God's procession is marching into the sanctuary. Who does David say leads the way?

cards.text: Singers up front, musicians right behind, with maidens playing tambourines all around. This is NOT a quiet entrance, friend. You can hear this crowd three streets over.

cards.question: True or false: Next, David calls for God to be blessed in the great congregation.

cards.text: There's Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them, with the princes of Judah, Zebulun and Naphtali, all tribes of Israel. Then David prays, "Summon Your power, O God; show Your strength, O God, which You have exerted on our behalf."

cards.question: David says that because of God's temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring Him ___.

cards.text: Then David asks God to rebuke the beast in the reeds and the herd of bulls among the calves of the nations, until it submits, bringing bars of silver.

cards.question: David asks God to scatter certain nations. Which ones?

answers.text: The ones who delight in war
The ones who live far away
The ones who trade with Egypt

cards.question: David says envoys will arrive from Egypt. What does he say Cush, a land south of Egypt, will do?

answers.text: Stretch out her hands to God
Send her armies to the north

cards.text: Then David calls the kingdoms of the earth to sing to God, who rides upon the highest heavens of old, whose mighty voice resounds. David's not inviting a couple of neighbors here; he's hitting reply-all on the WHOLE planet.

cards.question: True or false: David says God's majesty is over Israel, but His strength stays down on the earth.
In the final verse, David says the God of Israel Himself gives His people something. What?

cards.text: David tells God He is awesome in His sanctuary, and he closes with "Blessed be God!" Friend, after a parade like that, I'm ready to grab a tambourine and hop right into that procession, gold base and all.
